모델: M76 놀랐을 때 네 마디 — LAB 편 전체를 영상으로(제작 절차 lab-whole-video). 공통 글은 영상시험_20261125/지시문.json의 공통 글에서 그 편만의 소품(양머리 수건) · 빛 색을 빼고, 만화 효과 · 김 · 몸에서 튀어나옴을 막는 줄을 더했다(E64에서 팔 · 다리 · 입이 돋은 판). 11-25 15시 회차가 시작 그림을 위 벽까지 이어 구운 판(h*u)으로 바꾸고 사건을 앞 1초로 당겼다 — 11-25 21~23시: 공통 글을 영상_공통글.txt로 바꾸고(몽글 표정) h1 · h2 · h3 · h4 · h6을 표정이 있는 끝 그림으로 다시 굽는다. h5 · h5c는 바꾸기 앞 공통 글로 구워 통과한 판이다
공통: One continuous shot, no cuts. The camera is locked off exactly as in the start frame: no zoom, no pan, no tilt, no shake. Keep the exact handmade needle-felt miniature look of the start frame in every frame: fine wool felt fibres, visible stitches, matte felt and wool; every object keeps its shape, size and colour and never turns into a realistic thing. MONGLE is the coral-pink felt blob. At rest its face is only its two glossy black bead eyes: no nose and no mouth. When its feeling changes, its whole face changes to show that feeling, as written in ACTION, always in needle-felt: the eyes may grow bigger and rounder, squeeze shut into short curved dark stitched lines, curve into happy arcs or droop under little felt lids; a small simple felt mouth may open, smile, pout or wobble; blush, a felt sweat drop or a felt teardrop may appear. When the feeling passes, the mouth and the drops go away and the face returns to rest. Open eyes always stay glossy black beads: no white sclera, no eyelashes, no human teeth or lips. Mongle has NO arms, NO legs, NO hands and NO neck, ever: no limbs ever grow, nothing ever sticks out of its body. It moves only by tilting, squashing, stretching and bouncing its whole soft dome body. LOOK: the same light and colours as the start frame, unchanged to the last frame. Apart from Mongle's own expression, nothing new appears that is not in the start frame. No speed lines, no motion lines, no cartoon effects, no steam, no smoke. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos. No sound.

클립.prompt: Room 1 of the felt haunted house from the start frame: the closed mustard-yellow felt jack-in-the-box on the left and Mongle sitting on the teal floor on the right, its face at rest. ACTION: From 0 to 0.6 s Mongle leans its dome a little toward the closed box, curious. At about 0.7 s the teal lid flips open and the cream-white felt skeleton toy rises straight up out of the mustard box on its soft spring in half a second, its two felt arms up. At about 0.9 s Mongle tips its whole dome backward to the right, away from the box, and stays there, and its face changes to a big surprised face: its two black bead eyes become much bigger and perfectly round and a round open felt mouth of dark burgundy felt appears below them, with rosy cheeks, exactly as in the end frame. From 1.4 s to the end the skeleton toy sways gently left and right on its spring and Mongle stays leaned back with the same open-mouthed face, its dome slowly sinking and rising once like one deep breath; its hem stays flat on the floor. Mongle never grows arms or legs. The air and the wall around Mongle stay perfectly clean and empty in every frame: only the real felt objects of the start and end frames are ever visible, nothing is drawn over the picture.

Room 2 of the felt haunted house from the start frame: the white felt house ghost sitting on a little stool on the left with a bowl of felt noodles and chopsticks, Mongle on the right, its face at rest. ACTION: From 0 to 0.8 s the house ghost slurps a bundle of felt noodles, completely relaxed. At about 0.9 s it notices Mongle, turns its head toward Mongle and lifts one little felt hand in a lazy hello, then goes back to slurping noodles until the end. Mongle stays still and upright, staring at the ghost: at about 1.3 s its face changes to a dumbfounded deadpan face - two flat felt eyelids sink halfway over its bead eyes, a small straight stitched mouth appears below them and one small pale-blue felt sweat drop appears on the side of its head, exactly as in the end frame. From 1.6 s to the end Mongle keeps that flat look; at about 2.6 s it blinks once, slowly, and at about 3.2 s its half-closed eyes glance from the ghost to us. Mongle never grows arms or legs. The air and the wall around Mongle stay perfectly clean and empty in every frame: only the real felt objects of the start and end frames are ever visible, nothing is drawn over the picture.

Room 3 of the felt haunted house from the start frame: Mongle sitting alone on the floor with its face at rest, looking ahead, no spider in sight yet. ACTION: from 0 to 0.5 s Mongle looks around calmly. At about 0.6 s a big round fuzzy charcoal felt spider slides straight down its thread from above and comes to a stop just left of Mongle's face, hanging in the air with a clear gap from Mongle, never touching it and never going back up. At that same instant, in less than 0.3 s, Mongle's whole face cries out in fright: both eyes squeeze shut into two short dark stitched lines and a wide-open wobbly felt mouth of dark burgundy felt opens below them, its dome ducks low, its cheeks blush, and one small pale-blue felt teardrop appears by the eye on the right, exactly as in the end frame. From 1.3 s to the end Mongle keeps crying with its eyes squeezed shut and its mouth open, its body shaking in quick tiny moves, its hem always flat on the floor, while the spider hangs still on its straight thread and slowly wiggles its eight bendy felt legs. Mongle never grows arms or legs. No white wiggle lines, no shiver marks, no drawn marks around anything at any time.

Room 4 of the felt haunted house from the start frame: a night room with one dim amber lantern, the tall shut brown felt door on the left with a soft green glow under it, Mongle on the right with one small pale-blue felt teardrop. ACTION: From 0 to 0.5 s the lantern blinks once and comes back. From 0.3 to 1.3 s Mongle slides left across the floor to the shut door and pushes the bottom of the door two times with the front of its round body; the door stays firmly shut and does not move. From 1.4 s Mongle slides back to its place on the right and turns its face to the camera, and its face changes to a panicked, about-to-cry face: its black bead eyes become big and round, a wide wavy open felt mouth of dark burgundy felt appears below them, its cheeks turn rosy and a pale-blue felt teardrop hangs under each eye, exactly as in the end frame. From 2.2 s to the end it stays there with that face, its dome slowly sinking and rising as if sobbing, and the room gets a little brighter to match the end frame. Its hem is always flat on the floor. Mongle never grows arms or legs. The air and the wall around Mongle stay perfectly clean and empty in every frame: only the real felt objects of the start and end frames are ever visible, nothing is drawn over the picture.

The dark corner by the exit from the start frame: the young staff member in the white sheet-ghost cape with the hood pushed back, his face visible and a plain badge on his chest, peeking around the corner on the left; Mongle on the right, its coral wool softly glowing. ACTION: From 0 to 0.8 s the young man leans forward a little more, sneaking. At about 1.0 s he looks down and finds Mongle right beside him in the dark: his eyes go wide, his brows shoot up, he jumps backward with both hands up in fright, the cape flapping. From 1.8 to 3.2 s he spins around and scampers off to the left until he is completely out of the picture, the cape billowing behind him. Mongle stays sitting on the floor the whole time; from 3.4 s to the end Mongle is alone in the corner, slowly turns its dome toward the camera and blinks its bead eyes twice, puzzled. Mongle never grows arms or legs and never opens a mouth.

CLOSE-UP of the young staff member from the start frame, terrified, in the dark plum felt corner; a soft coral glow comes from low on the right, outside the frame. ACTION: at 0 s he is already frozen in a gasp, eyes wide, both open hands up beside his cheeks. From 0 to 0.8 s his raised hands jitter in quick tiny moves and his shoulders jerk back a little, his mouth stays open in the gasp, his eyes stay fixed on something low on the right. From 0.8 s to the end he keeps jittering and slowly sinks a little to the left, the cape shaking. He never smiles, never looks at the camera, his hands never touch his face. Mongle is not in this shot.

The last shot from the start frame: Mongle alone on the teal felt floor, facing the camera, its face at rest, the empty dark corner behind it. ACTION: from 0 to 0.8 s Mongle sits still, looking straight at us; at about 0.8 s it blinks its two bead eyes once. At about 1.2 s its dome tilts slowly to the left like a puzzled question and its face changes: its bead eyes become a little bigger, a small round open felt mouth appears, its cheeks turn rosy and one small pale-blue felt sweat drop appears on the side of its head, exactly as in the end frame. From 1.8 s to the end it keeps looking at us like that and blinks once more at about 2.3 s. Its hem is always flat on the floor. It never hops, never lifts off the floor, never slides. Mongle never grows arms or legs. The air and the wall around Mongle stay perfectly clean and empty in every frame: only the real felt objects of the start and end frames are ever visible, nothing is drawn over the picture.
